title: AI Coding Agents Are Breaking Big Codebases — Dan Adler, Sourcegraph
talk_summary: Sourcegraph's CEO argues AI-generated code volume is overwhelming large, long-lived codebases, and agents cannot understand what they cannot search. He pitches code-graph/search infrastructure and batch-change tooling that combines deterministic scripts with agents, CI/PR self-healing, and coverage auditing.

takeaways.technique: Code graph/search index for agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a compiler-accurate code graph plus search so agents can see cross-repo symbols, dependencies, and config references instead of relying on blind grep.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can't gp what you literally cannot see.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use deterministic scripts for mechanical edits across many repos and reserve coding agents for judgment-heavy steps, with tracking and auditability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Use coding agents where it makes sense, where judgment is needed. Use deterministic scripts where it's not.

takeaways.technique: Self-healing PR loop from CI and comments
takeaways.what_they_do: A batch-change agent iteratively responds to CI status and PR comments, pushing fixes until checks pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Self-heal respond to CI status PR comments.

takeaways.what_they_do: Track every repo or location where a patch is needed and audit that 100% of required places were covered.
takeaways.evidence_quote: provide tracking and auditability to be sure that you've covered 100% of the places where that patch is needed

takeaways.what_they_do: After fixing a known issue in a couple of repos, use an agent to explore the rest of the codebase for similar occurrences and patch them consistently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: go explore the rest of our codebase and found 80 other potential vulnerabilities
